high.title: The Fiverr Situation Gets Worse...
high.description:
Fiverr built its business on cheap freelance jobs. But what happens when AI can do more of that work in seconds? This video looks at how Fiverr went from a pandemic boom to a shrinking marketplace, with fewer buyers, falling revenue, and repeated cuts to its 2026 forecast. Back in 2020 and 2021, remote work sent demand soaring and pushed Fiverr’s stock to highs. Then offices reopened, growth slowed, and AI changed the economics of small gigs. Fiverr responded with AI categories, Fiverr Go, ads, subscriptions, and a workforce reduction. For a while, higher spending per buyer helped soften the damage. But as more customers left, that cushion started to wear thin. Now Fiverr is betting on larger, more complex projects and businesses willing to spend thousands of dollars. That means changing its search system, raising quality expectations, and convincing clients to see Fiverr as a place for serious work. Established sellers are feeling the disruption, while investors are asking whether the shift can happen fast enough. With the transformation expected to take at least six quarters, Fiverr’s future comes down to one question: can bigger projects replace the small jobs AI is taking away?

low.title: Apple Won…By Ignoring AI
low.description:
Try Mammouth now at http://mammouth.ai

For years, Apple was mocked for falling behind in AI. Siri was delayed, Apple Intelligence struggled to live up to the hype, competitors were spending hundreds of billions on data centers and GPUs, and some people were even questioning whether Apple still belonged in the Magnificent 7. Then something strange happened. Apple surged back toward the top of the market while spending a fraction of what companies like Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Google are pouring into AI. Instead of building massive AI infrastructure itself, Apple has taken a completely different approach: run as much AI as possible directly on its devices, use existing infrastructure for heavier workloads, and rent outside compute when necessary. That strategy looks even more powerful when you consider Apple already controls more than 2.5 billion active devices. While everyone else is fighting to build the best model and the biggest data centers, Apple may have realized that the most valuable part of AI is not the model at all. It is owning the customers, the hardware, and the ecosystem where AI actually gets used.
